links.outcome: Discrimination, calibration and net benefit of CVD models after recalibration or coefficient updating in older adults
links.effect: After updating, C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women; updated models showed good calibration and added net benefit at 4%-10% (women) and 5%-12% (men) thresholds.
links.quote: Following updating, the discrimination power of models increased for both sexes (C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women).

links.outcome: Generalization of models developed in middle-aged adults to older adults
links.effect: Models developed for middle-aged populations needed updating to improve prediction in older adults; further external validation in diverse older populations recommended before clinical implementation.
links.quote: Updating models, by adjusting model coefficients to better reflect the characteristics and risk factors of older adults, improves CVD risk prediction in a large cohort of relatively healthy Caucasian population aged 70+.
